title: Shadow kernel harness for per-layer quant-path evaluation and runtime heuristics
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background: We need a low-risk way to gather per-layer latency, memory, and fidelity signals for INT8/FP8/mixed-precision kernels in production-like workloads. Existing static heuristics mis-select quant paths for some models (cross-attention-heavy layers, long prefix decode) and the cost of dequant/requant overhead is significant in decode hot paths.

Goal: Implement a shadow-kernel harness that runs candidate quantized kernels in parallel (no side-effects) for a sampled subset of requests. Collect performance (p50/p95 latency, kernel execution time, KV cache pressure), numerical fidelity (kelly-score similarity, token-level divergence on small eval prompts), and dequantization overhead (bytes moved, memcpy time). Use signals to drive a runtime heuristic that chooses per-layer kernel paths (int8, fp8, fp16) and prefilling scheduling (staggered prefill vs unified prefill).

Non-goals: This ticket does not ship a global rollout policy — it exposes telemetry and a heuristics prototype. Full rollout engine and canary logic handled in follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow harness integrated into runtime with sampling configuration (1% default)
Collected telemetry for at least three production model families over 72h: KV memory metrics, per-kernel execution time, fidelity deltas
Heuristic prototype that consumes telemetry and recommends per-layer kernel path with a ruleset (latency + fidelity threshold)
Bench regression <1% tail latency for unshadowed requests; no functional change to inference outputs
Documentation (runtime/ops playbook) and one PR merged with tests and feature flag gating
tasks: Design shadow API and feature flag gating (runtime-safe, off-by-default)
Implement non-blocking shadow executor with bounded concurrency and memory caps
Add fidelity metric collectors (log-prob delta, token agreement) and lightweight sketch for distributional diffs
Instrument KV cache metrics and memory pressure signals
Wire telemetry to internal metrics pipeline (Grafana dashboards + long-term trace events)
Prototype heuristic evaluator and offline tool to recommend per-layer paths from collected data
End-to-end tests, performance safety tests, and a canary plan doc
comments: 2026-03-10 Ava Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached (Confluence /drive link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Shadow+Kernels). Agreed sampling default 1% and max-memory-overhead 12%.

2026-03-12 Maya Chen (review): Requested stronger isolation between shadow and primary KV cache to prevent eviction interference. Suggested adding a per-request tag and bounded ephemeral slab allocator.

2026-03-13 Diego Rivera: Implemented tracer for fidelity metrics. Early runs on small Llama-variant: shadow int8 kernel showed 1.6% token-distribution KL divergence vs fp16 baseline; p95 kernel time reduced by 28ms on decode-heavy prompts. Detailed microbench: https://perf.redwood.ai/bench/56011-2026-03-13

2026-03-14 Ava Patel: Ran 72-hour sampling across two internal model families. Observations: cross-attention dominated layers favor fp16/FP8 hybrid — candidate heuristic: prefer int8 when KL < 0.5% and p95 kernel time improvement > 20ms and cache pressure delta < 6%. Next: build offline recommender to export ruleset and integrate into runtime selector.
